.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Cool and dry weather continues through the weekend,
although a slow-moving Nor'easter off the coast will bring gusty
winds along the Chesapeake Bay and minor tidal flooding at times
through Friday.

The position of the Nor'easter hasn't changed much from
yesterday at this time, a few hundred miles east-southeast of
Cape Hatteras. Strong high pressure builds toward Quebec tonight
into Tuesday, while the low starts to drift northward as the 
preceding northern stream shortwave causes a weakness in the 
block. This will lead to a greater pressure gradient and 
slightly breezier conditions Tuesday. For tonight, that also 
means fewer areas will become calm. In addition, dew points will
be higher where the growing season continues, so frost appears 
unlikely tonight.

The ridge will continue to expand north and west of the low,
blocking it from substantial movement through mid week. Although
some uncertainty remains in the exact track/timing of the 
Nor'easter, this pattern will keep the low far enough off the 
coast to eliminate rain potential (and clouds for that matter) 
across the forecast area. Overall, any impacts will be tied to 
coastal communities along the Chesapeake Bay where potential 
minor coastal flooding and gusty marine winds remain possible 
concerns this week. More information on those topics is included
in sections below.

Temperatures will climb slightly through mid week, ending up on
either side of normal values.

By Thursday, what remains of the upper reflection of the offshore 
closed low gradually becomes absorbed into a deep trough over 
eastern Canada. These adjoining features are slated to pull eastward 
into the Canadian Maritimes while upstream heights build across the 
Mississippi Valley. From Friday and into this weekend, this broad 
ridge axis advances eastward ahead of a trough inhabiting the 
western/central U.S. As this occurs, there are some hints of another 
upper low center getting pinched off near the Carolina coast. 
However, its far southward displacement should minimize any direct 
impacts from this system. Overall synoptic uncertainty does increase 
markedly toward the end of the weekend and into early next week. 
Most notably, it revolves around a split in the jet streams over the 
middle of the continent. 

Looking down at the surface, a fresh area of high pressure
behind the departing trough/Canadian cold front dominates 
through late week while becoming more centered over the 
northeastern U.S. by Saturday. This ensures continued tranquil 
weather heading toward the last week of October. Expect dry 
conditions along with abundant sunshine each day. The air mass 
will remain quite dry owing to the prevailing northerly 
component to the local wind fields. Most days should yield highs
in the 60s (50s for the mountains). The coldest overnight 
periods will likely be Friday and Saturday nights as lows fall 
into the 30s to low 40s. With the growing season having ended 
from the Blue Ridge westward, it remains to be seen if any 
frost/freeze threats emerge off to the east.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
VFR conditions continue through the end of the week as surface 
high pressure builds north of the area and dry conditions 
persist. Winds remain primarily out of the north each day, 
gusting around 15-20 knots at times each afternoon. As high 
pressure settles overhead, winds turn lighter by Saturday.

&&

.MARINE...
The Nor'easter off the Mid-Atlantic coast will remain the
prominent weather feature through Friday. This will result in
nearly continuous Small Craft Advisory conditions in northerly
flow over the middle Chesapeake Bay, while northern and 
interior waters will occasionally see breaks.

Expect a northerly wind to largely dominate Wednesday through 
Friday before turning more northeasterly by the night. Small 
Craft Advisories may be needed on Thursday, but particularly by 
late Thursday into Friday morning given a northerly surge in the
winds.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal anomalies will rise again through midweek as a Nor'easter
starts drifting northward offshore. Tidal locations including 
Dahlgren, Annapolis, Solomons Island, and Alexandria are 
forecast to reach minor flood stage by Tuesday night or 
Wednesday high tide cycles. Annapolis could approach moderate 
flood stage. However, some uncertainty remains on how exactly 
this Nor'easter will affect the tide levels. Elevated water 
levels likely won't decline until late in the week when the low 
will finally start pulling out to sea.
